plmm.readme:
# Product Landscape Meta-Model (PLMM)

A structured, Git-native, AI-ready model of the whole product landscape — the federation layer above AISMM.

## Contents - [What is PLMM?](#what-is-plmm) - [PLMM and AISMM](#plmm-and-aismm) - [Why PLMM is needed](#why-plmm-is-needed) - [What PLMM gives you](#what-plmm-gives-you) - [How PLMM is structured](#how-plmm-is-structured) · [The eleven layers](#the-eleven-layers) - [Layer document model](#layer-document-model) - [Repository-native by design](#repository-native-by-design) - [PLMM and AI agents](#plmm-and-ai-agents) - [What PLMM is not](#what-plmm-is-not) - [Status & roadmap](#status--roadmap) - [License](#license) ## What is PLMM? **PLMM (Product Landscape Meta-Model)** is a structured, machine-readable and human-readable way to describe an entire **portfolio of products** as one connected system. Where [AISMM](https://github.com/orkestron-ai/software-meta-model) models a *single* software product in full context, PLMM models the **landscape between products**: the registry, the dependency and integration graph, shared capabilities, cross-product processes, ownership and governance, and how each product's AISMM is federated into one navigable whole. In simple terms: ```text AISMM = full structured context of ONE product PLMM = full structured context of the PRODUCT LANDSCAPE (many products + how they relate) ``` It is designed to be stored in Git, reviewed like code, used by humans, and traversed by AI agents that need to know *which* products and *which* AISMM models a task touches. --- ## Core model PLMM frames the enterprise as a single chain of context, from the whole landscape down to a single product's full-context model: ```text Enterprise Landscape → PLMM → Product → AISMM ``` Everything in PLMM is expressed with five core entities: | Entity | What it represents | |--------|--------------------| | **Product** | A business/technical asset in the landscape (identity, lifecycle, ownership). | | **Product Relationship** | A typed edge between products — dependency, integration, event or data flow. | | **Capability** | A business capability, mapped to the product(s) that own or share it. | | **Cross-Product Process** | A process that spans several products and the models it needs. | | **AISMM Reference** | A federation link from a product into its own AISMM model. | --- ## PLMM and AISMM PLMM does not replace AISMM — it **federates** it. ```text ┌──────────────────────────── PLMM ────────────────────────────┐ │ Product registry · graph · capabilities · processes · │ │ operations · governance · semantic routing · portfolio │ └───────┬───────────────────┬───────────────────┬───────────────┘ │ federates │ federates │ federates ┌───▼───┐ ┌───▼───┐ ┌───▼───┐ │ AISMM │ │ AISMM │ │ AISMM │ ← one per product │ prod A│ │ prod B│ │ prod C│ └───────┘ └───────┘ └───────┘ ``` - Each product keeps its own **AISMM** (b0–b12) as the source of truth for that product. - PLMM holds only **landscape-level** facts and **references** into each AISMM (see the [AISMM Federation layer](./07-federation/aismm-federation.layer.md)) — never a copy. - An agent enters at PLMM, resolves *which products and contexts* a task spans (see [Semantic Routing](./10-semantic-routing/semantic-routing.layer.md)), then loads the relevant AISMM models. --- ## Why PLMM is needed A single product is well described by AISMM. But an organization rarely has one product — it has a **landscape**: - many products and services, owned by different teams - dependencies, integrations, events and data flows between them - capabilities that are shared, duplicated or missing - business processes that span several products at once - one product replacing, extending or deprecating another over time - a need to know, for any change, *what else it touches* Without a landscape model this knowledge lives in people's heads, slide decks and stale diagrams. PLMM makes it **explicit, versioned and queryable** — the same way AISMM does for a single product. --- ## What PLMM gives you - **Product Registry** — every product as a first-class, identified asset. - **Product Graph** — dependencies, integrations, events and data exchange. - **Capability Landscape** — who owns what, what's shared, where the gaps are. - **Cross-Product Processes** — flows that span multiple products and the models they need. - **AISMM Federation** — a contract binding each product's AISMM into the landscape. - **Semantic Routing** — a deterministic answer to "which contexts must I load?" - **Landscape Governance** — ownership, accountability, risk and compliance across the portfolio. --- ## How PLMM is structured PLMM is organized as **eleven layers**, each answering a distinct set of questions about the landscape. Layers are folders; each holds one or more `*.layer.md` documents. ### The eleven layers | # | Layer | Answers | |---|-------|---------| | 01 | [Product Profile](./01-products/product-profile.layer.md) | What is each product, why does it exist, who owns it? | | 02 | [Product Relationships](./02-relationships/product-relationships.layer.md) | How do products depend on, integrate with and feed each other? | | 03 | [Capability Landscape](./03-capabilities/capability-landscape.layer.md) | Which product owns which capability; what is shared? | | 04 | [Cross-Product Processes](./04-processes/cross-product-processes.layer.md) | Which products and AISMM models does a process span? | | 05 | [Operations](./05-operations/operations.layer.md) | Where each product runs (hosting, FQDN, VLAN), how it's monitored, backed up, and its SLA? | | 06 | [Governance](./06-governance/governance.layer.md) | Who is accountable (Product / Business / Engineering Owner); what risk and compliance applies? | | 07 | [AISMM Federation](./07-federation/aismm-federation.layer.md) | Which AISMM belongs to a product; what is exposed? | | 08 | [Change & Evolution](./08-change/change-evolution.layer.md) | What changed across the landscape; what replaced what? | | 09 | [Consistency & Trust](./09-consistency/consistency-trust.layer.md) | Is information verified; what is its source and coverage? | | 10 | [Semantic Routing](./10-semantic-routing/semantic-routing.layer.md) | Which contexts and AISMM models must a task load? | | 11 | [Portfolio Landscape](./11-portfolio/portfolio-landscape.layer.md) | How do products roll up into groups and business units? | The portfolio hierarchy PLMM describes: ```text Business Unit └─ Product Group └─ Product └─ AISMM (the product's own full-context model) ``` --- ## Layer document model Every layer document is plain Markdown and follows the same shape, so humans and parsers read it the same way: ```markdown # ## Purpose ## Questions ## Blocks / Structure ``` Keep landscape *facts and references* here; keep product *internals* in that product's AISMM. When a layer is intentionally not filled yet, say so explicitly rather than leaving it blank. --- ## Repository-native by design PLMM is a **specification**, not a package to install. A landscape model lives in a Git repository: - folders are layers, documents are Markdown — diff and review like code - references into product AISMM repos are links, not copies - history is the landscape's evolution; pull requests are how it changes This makes the landscape model versioned, auditable and mergeable — the same properties AISMM gives a single product. --- ## PLMM and AI agents An AI agent working across products needs to know the blast radius of a task *before* it starts. PLMM gives it a deterministic entry point: 1. Enter at the **Product Graph** and **Semantic Routing** layers. 2. Resolve which products, capabilities and processes the task spans. 3. Follow the **AISMM Federation** references to load exactly the product models needed — no more, no less. This keeps agent context **scoped and explainable**: the model decides what to load, and you can trace why. --- ## What PLMM is not - It is **not** a replacement for AISMM — it sits above it and references it. - It is **not** a copy of product internals — only landscape facts and links. - It is **not** a CMDB lock-in or a diagramming tool — it is a Git-native, AI-readable knowledge model. - It is **not** a runtime — execution lives in the products themselves. --- ## Status & roadmap PLMM is an early **draft (v0.1.0)**: the eleven layers and their questions are defined; field-level schemas, a landscape registry format, consistency rules and validation tooling are the next steps — mirroring how AISMM matured. Feedback and proposals are welcome via issues and pull requests. --- ## License Licensed under the [Apache License 2.0](./LICENSE). See [NOTICE](./NOTICE). Part of the [Orkestron](https://github.com/orkestron-ai) ecosystem: PLMM is the landscape-level model that complements [AISMM](https://github.com/orkestron-ai/software-meta-model) (per product) and feeds [Full-Context Development (FCD)](https://github.com/orkestron-ai/full-context-development). · [orkestron.ai](https://orkestron.ai/)

aismm.readme_head:
# AI-driven Software Meta-Model (AISMM)

A structured, Git-native, AI-ready product knowledge model for full-context software development.

## Contents - [What is AISMM?](#what-is-aismm) - [Quick start](#quick-start) - [Why AISMM is needed](#why-aismm-is-needed) - [Core idea](#core-idea) · [What AISMM gives you](#what-aismm-gives-you) - [How AISMM is structured](#how-aismm-is-structured) · [Bundles (b0–b12)](#bundles) - [Canonical product model layout](#canonical-product-model-layout) · [Document model](#document-model) - [Repository-native by design](#repository-native-by-design) · [Machine-readable schemas](#machine-readable-schemas) - [AISMM and AI agents](#aismm-and-ai-agents) · [AISMM and RAG](#aismm-and-rag) - [What's new in v3.1](#aismm-v31-additions) · [v3 additions](#aismm-v3-additions) · [v2 additions](#aismm-v2-additions) - [How AISMM relates to other approaches](#how-aismm-relates-to-other-approaches) - [What AISMM is not](#what-aismm-is-not) · [Versioning and conformance](#versioning-and-conformance) - [FAQ](#faq) - [Contributing & community](#contributing--community) · [License](#license) ## What is AISMM? **AISMM (AI-driven Software Meta-Model)** is a structured, machine-readable and human-readable way to describe a software product as a complete system. It is not just documentation. AISMM is a **product knowledge model** that connects: - why the product exists - what business value it creates - how the system is designed - how behavior is specified - how the code is implemented - how the system runs in production - how quality, risk and compliance are controlled - how changes are planned and released - how knowledge is indexed, traced and trusted In simple terms: ```text AISMM = full structured context of a software product ``` It is designed to be stored in Git, reviewed like code, used by humans, and processed by AI agents. --- ## AISMM at a glance

AISMM connects value, system design, execution and knowledge into a unified model for AI-driven software engineering.

--- ## Quick start AISMM is a **specification**, not a package to install. "Getting started" means putting a product's knowledge under the model. The fastest path: 1. **Vendor the meta-model into your product repo.** Add this canon as `00-meta/software-meta-model-main/` (and the template tree alongside it) so your repo carries the rules it conforms to. See [Canonical product model layout](#canonical-product-model-layout). 2. **Create the registry.** Copy [`examples/aismm.registry.example.json`](./examples/aismm.registry.example.json) to `aismm.registry.json` at your repo root and fill in your `product_id` and sources. Parsers and agents start from this file — see [`aismm-model-registry.md`](./aismm-model-registry.md). 3. **Stand up the bundle/layer folders** under `aismm/` (b0–b12). For any layer you'll need but haven't filled yet, drop an **explicit empty-layer block** instead of leaving it missing — copy [`examples/empty-layer.example.md`](./examples/empty-layer.example.md). See [Empty layers vs missing layers](#empty-layers-vs-missing-layers). 4. **Write your first real layer** — a good start is `b0.001` (product definition) or `b4.401` (requirements). Add the AISMM block header (see [Document model](#document-model)) and link it to related entities. 5. **Validate and declare a level.** Run the consistency and health checks ([`aismm-consistency-checks.md`](./aismm-consistency-checks.md), [`aismm-health.md`](./aismm-health.md)) and declare a [conformance level](#versioning-and-conformance) — start at L1. > New to the concepts? Read [What is AISMM?](#what-is-aismm) and > [Core idea](#core-idea) first, then come back here. --- ## Why AISMM is needed Modern software products are not just code. A real product includes: - business goals - value streams - stakeholders - requirements - architecture - data models - APIs - integrations - processes - UX scenarios - runtime infrastructure - monitoring - incidents - tests - risks - security controls - release history - decisions - hidden context in tasks and discussions Most companies keep this knowledge scattered across many systems: ```text Jira + Git + Confluence + Figma + BPMN + Grafana + CI/CD + Slack + people's heads ``` This creates several problems: - AI agents cannot understand the full product context. - New developers need too much time to understand the system. - Architecture decisions lose their original reasoning. - Requirements drift away from implementation. - Tests are not clearly linked to behavior. - Incidents are not clearly linked to releases and changes. - Product value is disconnected from technical work. - Knowledge becomes too large, noisy and hard to retrieve. AISMM solves this by turning scattered product knowledge into a **connected semantic model**. --- ## Core idea AISMM treats a software system as: ```text Value + Structure + Behavior + Execution + Change + Knowledge ``` Or more explicitly: ```text Software System = Business Value + Product Behavior + System Design + Implementation + Runtime Reality + Quality / Risk / Compliance + SDLC History + Traceable Knowledge ``` This allows both humans and AI agents to reason about the product as a whole. --- ## What AISMM gives you

model.purpose: Compose client-isolated infrastructure and service references with explicit authoritative data routing.
model.scope_statement: A bounded service-provider/client graph profile. It records tenant boundary, service/asset references, dependencies, desired versus observed state, per-fact mastership, routed change outcomes, and authorized projections. It does not become a competing CMDB or authorization engine.
in_scope: Per-fact owning Dimension and master-system mapping
out_of_scope: Full asset, party, ownership, task or contract lifecycles
Implemented IAM, CMDB, discovery, Jira connector or distributed transaction engine
Automatic legal ownership transfer or proof of client acceptance
Universal infrastructure schema or full Redfish conformance

Reference typed dependency semantics; domain profile supplies tenant/master boundaries, not universal impact calculus.

Link work IDs; do not copy task state as an independently editable authority.
